title: Military service, wartime and the disguised German records
summary: Military service from 1938 ended his listening. In 1944-45 he found German-labelled records in a house in Germany that turned out to be Benny Goodman jazz.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. Did, how long did this last that you could listen to jazz? Was it interrupted? Stopped?

Um, it was very, very nice, uh, time until, uh, 38, because it was, uh, the time when comes clothes over Europe, and I began my military service, and that was the end of my music, um, interests. Of course, not, uh, exactly, uh, interest, but no possibility to hear except military music. As you can imagine, it is not the same. It was 38, uh, and very, I have very hard, uh, my military service before Hitler came to Poland. Poland, and only, uh, twice when I've been on a vaca-, not vacation, it is a special possibility to come home for one or two days.

Yes. Uh, immediately after, uh, immediately in the same evening I must to hear jazz music in nightclubs, because it was something like hunger. Everybody, everybody can understand such a situation. And then was interruption, uh, a few years of war. Uh, and I have very, uh, funny, uh, incident during the war. When I have been the second time in military, in 44 and 45, once, I've been in the Germany, um, before the end of the war, with the army. As you know, from one side, uh, Anglo-American army, and I was in the army, Polish army, that was together with the Russian army. And in one house, when we stopped for one night, I found a few German records, and one of these records was, uh, Benny Goodman group, and one record was Nelson Eddy and Janet MacDonald. But the cover of this record has a German, uh, print, uh, mark, with another names of, uh, composers, and names of, uh, compositions, and names of interpreters, uh, of, uh, musicians. Uh, of course, uh, German musicians. It was, uh, Haydn, um, it was this mark of, of record, was, uh, hidden or Haydn, how it is? Yes, hidden. Hidden. And only owner of this, uh, of, of this apartment that was not here in this moment, he is gone. Uh, only the owner, uh, knew about that, uh, mystification. And it was a very happy moment for me when I put this record, plenty of records on the gramophone, and we make this whole story true, that it is a jazz record and pop record from America, because American music was prohibited in Germany during Hitler, especially jazz, because they called jazz music of Negro, and Negro was the enemy of the race, pure race of Germans. So it is one of accident during the war. And next it is another story, maybe you have more questions.
